core_obligations: Reduce to an affine base T and then to the case where X carries a surjective etale morphism U -> X from an affine scheme U (proof lines 10820-10841).
Show that U -> T is quasi-finite and that R = U x_X U is an affine scheme whose two projections are etale, quasi-finite, flat and of finite presentation (proof lines 10849-10865).
Check that the seven hypotheses of the More on Groupoids quasi-finiteness lemma hold for the groupoid (U, R, s, t, c) over T at the chosen pair (u, p) (proof lines 10868-10876).

Apply that lemma to obtain an etale neighbourhood (T', p') with kappa(p) = kappa(p'), the decompositions U_{T'} = U' disjoint union W and R_{T'} = R' disjoint union W', and conclusions (a)-(h) (proof lines 10877-10887).
Deduce from conclusion (h) that R' = U' x_{X_{T'}} U' and that (g) gives an etale equivalence relation, so that U'/R' is an open subspace of X_{T'} (proof lines 10888-10893).

Conclude that U' and R' are affine with finite etale projections, so U'/R' is an affine scheme, and finish with the neighbourhood-scheme lemma and the local character of representability (proof lines 10894-10911).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Proposition: for a morphism f : X -> T of algebraic spaces over a scheme S with T representable, f locally quasi-finite and f separated, the algebraic space X is representable (source lines 10806-10817). The proof is a multi-stage reduction that cannot be replaced by a citation: it reduces to an affine base by a Zariski covering, then to the case where an affine U maps surjectively etale onto X, forms the etale equivalence relation R = U x_X U presenting X as U/R, checks the seven hypotheses of the More on Groupoids quasi-finiteness lemma for the groupoid (U, R, s, t, c) over T at a chosen pair of points (u, p), and applies it to obtain an etale neighbourhood (T', p') and a disjoint union decomposition whose affine quotient U'/R' is an open subspace of X_{T'}. The closing step turns this local affine neighbourhood into a global representability statement via the neighbourhood-scheme lemma.
